newsitem.title: USA: Schering Intron A extended therapy approved.
newsitem.headline: Schering Intron A extended therapy approved.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said Wednesday it has received marketing clearance for its Intron A drug from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for extended therapy of 18 to 24 months for chronic viral hepatitis C.
Intron A, an injectable drug, had been previously cleared for six months' therapy to treat chronic hepatitis B and C.
The drug has been marketed in the U.S. since 1991 and is also sold in 68 countries.

Schering-Plough said it conducted two independent clinical studies to support its application to extend the drug's therapy period and results were compared with those obtained in the six-month course of therapy.

"The combined results...demonstrated that 24 percent of all patients treated for 18 to 24 months achieved a durable sustained response compared with 12.5 percent for those treated for six months," the company said.
Schering-Plough said that data from the Atlanta-based Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show that between 4.0 to 4.5 million Americans are chronically infected with hepatitis C virus.
Because symptoms are not often detectable at early stages, a great majority of infected people are unaware of the ailment until they develop seious liver complications, the company said.
Hepatitis C infection contributes to the death of more than 12,000 Americans each year, it added.

Richard Zahn, president of Schering Laboratories, the pharmaceutical arm of Schering-Plough, said, "The FDA's prompt action on this extended-dosing submission now provides physicians with the opportunity to develop optimal therapy for their hepatitis C patients."
"Patients who are diagnosed early and treated for a duration of 18 to 24 months have a better chance of maintaining a long-term response," he added.
